current_example.title: Example: Finding an Orthogonal Projection Matrix Given Vectors That Span the Orthogonal Complement

q-95188.name: Question 1
q-95188.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
q-95188.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =(21)^{-1}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{21}[\begin{aligned}16 & 4 & 8 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 8 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-40131.name: Question 2
q-40131.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
q-40131.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & ={6}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-40131.html:
Question 2
?

Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of R3 onto the subspace spanned by a=[−112].

a
 19[1−12−11−22−24]
b
118[1−1−4−112−421]
c
16[1−1−2−112−224]
d
 19[4−1−4−112−423]
e
 16[4−1−2−142−221]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that the matrix PS=A(ATA)−1AT maps any vector x∈Rn onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace S spanned by the columns of the matrix A.

In our case, A=[−112]. Therefore,

PS=A(ATA)−1AT=[−112]([−112][−112])−1[−112]=6−1[−112][−112]=16[1−1−2−112−224].

q-40648.name: Question 3
q-40648.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$
q-40648.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & ={29}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{29}[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & 12 \\ 6 & 4 & 8 \\ 12 & 8 & 16\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-40128.name: Question 4
q-40128.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
q-40128.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =(14)^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}9 & -6 & 3 \\ -6 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-40128.html:
Question 4
?

Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of R3 onto the subspace spanned by a=[3−21].

a
 114[9−63−64−23−21]
b
 114[1−69−642921]
c
 17[6−33−33−43−41]
d
 114[1−24−296463]
e
 14[9−43−44−13−11]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that the matrix PS=A(ATA)−1AT maps any vector x∈Rn onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace S spanned by the columns of the matrix A.

In our case, A=[3−21]. Therefore,

PS=A(ATA)−1AT=[3−21]([3−21][3−21])−1[3−21]=(14)−1[3−21][3−21]=114[9−63−64−23−21].

q-95147.name: Question 5
q-95147.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
q-95147.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =(6)^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-95147.html:
Question 5
?

Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of R3 onto the subspace spanned by a=[2−11].

a
14[4−21−2−1111−1]
b
14[−21−11−22−121]
c
16[−21−11−22−121]
d
13[4−22−21−12−11]
e
16[4−22−21−12−11]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that the matrix PS=A(ATA)−1AT maps any vector x∈Rn onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace S spanned by the columns of the matrix A.

In our case, A=[2−11]. Therefore,

PS=A(ATA)−1AT=[2−11]([2−11][2−11])−1[2−11]=(6)−1[2−11][2−11]=16[4−22−21−12−11].

q-95334.name: Question 6
q-95334.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $r=sv+tw$, where

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$
q-95334.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $r=sv+tw$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}\{v,w\}.$ 
Hence, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & -4 \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-5 & -4 & 2 \\ 4 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & 5 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-40647.name: Question 7
q-40647.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $r=sv+tw$, where

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$
q-40647.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $r=sv+tw$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}\{v,w\}.$ 
Hence, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-40665.name: Question 8
q-40665.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $r=sv+tw$, where

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$
q-40665.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $r=sv+tw$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}\{v,w\}.$ 
Hence, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}6 & 1 \\ 1 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{35}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 & -1 \\ -1 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{35}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 4 & 13 \\ 5 & 11 & -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{35}[\begin{aligned}10 & 15 & 5 \\ 15 & 26 & -3 \\ 5 & -3 & 34\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-95332.name: Question 9
q-95332.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $r=sv+tw$, where

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
q-95332.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $r=sv+tw$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}\{v,w\}.$ 
Hence, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-95332.html:
Question 9
?

Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of R3 onto the plane whose parametric equation is r=sv+tw, where v=[−101],w=[111].

a
16[12−5211−512]
b
12[12−5211−512]
c
16[52−1222−125]
d
13[220222023]
e
13[52−5222−521]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that the matrix PS=A(ATA)−1AT maps any vector x∈Rn onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace S spanned by the columns of the matrix A.

Notice that the plane r=sv+tw is actually the subspace Span{v,w}. Hence, we have A=[−110111]. Therefore, PS=A(ATA)−1AT=[−110111]([−101111][−110111])−1[−101111]=[−110111][2003]−1[−101111]=16[−110111][3002][−101111]=16[−110111][−303222]=16[52−1222−125].

q-95204.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $r=sv+tw$, where

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$
q-95204.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $r=sv+tw$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}\{v,w\}.$ 
Hence, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 14\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{27}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}14 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{27}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & -16 & 11 \\ 2 & 5 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{27}[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & 26 & -1 \\ 5 & -1 & 26\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the matrix PS=A(ATA)−1AT maps any vector x∈Rn onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace S spanned by the columns of the matrix A.

q-95342.name: Question 11
q-95342.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

I. ${A}^{T}=A$

II. ${A}^{2}=A$

III. $A$ is an orthogonal projection matrix
q-95342.worked_solution:
Recall that $Q$ is an orthogonal projection matrix if and only if ${Q}^{2}=Q$ and ${Q}^{T}=Q.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine each of the statements in turn.

- Statement I is false since ${A}^{T}\ne A.$

- Statement II is true. Indeed, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{2} & =A\cdot A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is false since not both statements I and II are true.

Therefore, the correct answer is " II only."

q-95352.name: Question 13
q-95352.problem:
Which of the following are orthogonal projection matrices?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & \frac{2}{3} \\ -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2} & \frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{3}{4} & -\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{13} & \frac{6}{13} \\ \frac{6}{13} & \frac{4}{13}\end{aligned}].
$$
q-95352.worked_solution:
Recall that $Q$ is an orthogonal projection matrix if and only if ${Q}^{2}=Q$ and ${Q}^{T}=Q.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- $A$ is *not* an orthogonal projection matrix. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\ne A.\end{aligned}
$$

- $B$ is *not* an orthogonal projection matrix. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{T}\ne B.\end{aligned}
$$

- $C$ is an orthogonal projection matrix. Indeed,
${C}^{T}=C$
and

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{2} & =C\cdot C \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{13} & \frac{6}{13} \\ \frac{6}{13} & \frac{4}{13}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{13} & \frac{6}{13} \\ \frac{6}{13} & \frac{4}{13}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{13}[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 \\ 6 & 4\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{13}[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 \\ 6 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{169}[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 \\ 6 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & 6 \\ 6 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{169}[\begin{aligned}117 & 78 \\ 78 & 52\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{13} & \frac{6}{13} \\ \frac{6}{13} & \frac{4}{13}\end{aligned}] \\  & =C.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$C$ only."

q-40164.name: Question 16
q-40164.problem:
$$
a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,P=\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}{p}_{11} & {p}_{12} & {p}_{13} \\ {p}_{21} & {p}_{22} & {p}_{23} \\ {p}_{31} & {p}_{32} & {p}_{33}\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that the vector $a$ above spans ${S}^{⊥},$ and that $P$ is the orthogonal projection matrix of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace $S$, what is the value of ${p}_{22}+{p}_{31}?$
q-40164.worked_solution:
First, we find the orthogonal projection matrix onto ${S}^{⊥}=\text{Span}\{a\}.$

Using the formula for the orthogonal projection matrix

$$
{P}_{{S}^{⊥}}=a({a}^{T}\,a)^{-1}{a}^{T},
$$

we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{{S}^{⊥}} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & ={9}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & -4 \\ -2 & 1 & 2 \\ -4 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that ${P}_{S}+{P}_{{S}^{⊥}}=I.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =I-{P}_{{S}^{⊥}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & -4 \\ -2 & 1 & 2 \\ -4 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 8 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, ${p}_{22}+{p}_{31}=8+4=12.$

q-95363.html:
Question 20
?

a=[1−12],P=16[p11p12p13p21p22p23p31p32p33] Given that the vector a above spans S⊥, and that P is the orthogonal projection matrix of R3 onto the subspace S, what is the value of p12+p33?

a
7
b
4
c
−4
d
3
e
−1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the orthogonal projection matrix onto S⊥=Span{a}.

Using the formula for the orthogonal projection matrix

PS⊥=a(aTa)−1aT,

we obtain the following:

PS⊥=[1−12]([1−12][1−12])−1[1−12]=6−1[1−12][1−12]=16[1−12−11−22−24]

Recall that PS+PS⊥=I. Therefore,

PS=I−PS⊥=[100010001]−16[1−12−11−22−24]=16[51−2152−222].

Finally, p12+p33=1+2=3.
